title: Add a new row with INSERT
description: Write a statement that inserts a new department named `'Legal'` into the `departments` table.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: INSERT INTO ... VALUES
INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values) adds one new row - id is a SERIAL column here, so it fills itself in automatically if you don't specify it.
Name just the name column in your INSERT (skip id entirely) and give it the single value 'Legal'.
explanation: Naming the column list explicitly (INSERT INTO departments (name) ...) means the statement doesn't depend on knowing every column's position - the SERIAL id column is left out entirely and Postgres assigns it.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT name FROM departments WHERE name = 'Legal'
